fields.add_help: Add another voice to the ensemble (2 to 8 voices).

columns.help: Name of this voice, e.g. Soprano. Free text.
columns.label: Name

columns.help: Lowest note this voice may sing, inclusive (note name or MIDI number).
columns.label: Low

columns.help: Highest note this voice may sing, inclusive (note name or MIDI number).
columns.label: High

columns.help: Which staff of a grand-staff chord sheet this voice is drawn on. Auto picks treble or bass from the voice's range; Treble/Bass pins it.
columns.label: Staff

fields.label: Voices
fields.remove_help: Remove this voice from the ensemble.

fields.help: Maximum semitone gap allowed between each pair of neighbouring voices; comma-separated, one value per gap.
fields.label: Max spacing

fields.help: Whether two neighbouring voices may land on the same pitch.
fields.label: Allow unisons

sections.blurb: Each weight adds to a voicing's score, so a higher number always means more preferred. Positive values pull the picker toward a trait; negative values push it away. Zero is neutral. The defaults suit most music, so change these only if the results aren't to your taste.

fields.help: How the picker treats an inner or upper voice moving between chords, per semitone (a single number, or one per voice, top first). More negative discourages movement; positive would encourage it.
fields.label: Voice movement

fields.help: How the picker treats the bottom voice moving between chords, per semitone; normally set less negative than the inner-voice movement weight. Ignored when Voice movement lists one value per voice.
fields.label: Bass movement

fields.help: How the picker treats a voice jumping more than a fifth between chords. More negative avoids large leaps.
fields.label: Large leap

fields.help: How the picker treats a voice jumping more than an octave, on top of the large-leap weight. More negative avoids octave leaps.
fields.label: Octave leap

fields.help: How the picker treats a voice leaping exactly a tritone (six semitones). More negative avoids tritone leaps.
fields.label: Tritone leap

fields.help: How the picker treats a voice singing the same note again (same pitch, same octave) on the next chord. More positive rewards holding common tones.
fields.label: Common tone held

fields.help: How the picker treats a pair of voices moving in parallel fifths or octaves. More negative avoids them; set strongly negative by default.
fields.label: Parallel fifths/octaves

fields.help: How the picker treats the outer two voices moving in opposite directions. More positive encourages it.
fields.label: Contrary motion

fields.help: How the picker treats a chordal seventh resolving down by step. More positive encourages that resolution.
fields.label: Seventh resolves down

fields.help: How the picker treats the leading tone rising a semitone to the tonic, in the same voice. Only applies when the song sets a key. More positive encourages it.
fields.label: Leading tone resolves

fields.help: How the picker treats two or more voices on the leading tone. Only applies when the song sets a key. More negative avoids doubling it.
fields.label: Doubled leading tone

fields.help: How the picker treats a voice sitting in the outer 2 semitones of its range, per semitone into that edge. More negative keeps voices off their extremes.
fields.label: Out-of-comfort range

fields.help: How the picker treats a pair of neighbouring voices on the same pitch, when unisons are allowed. More negative avoids unisons.
fields.label: Unison between voices

fields.help: How the picker treats a gap wider than a fifth (7 semitones) between two neighbouring voices above the bass, per semitone beyond it. More negative favors closer spacing above the bass.
fields.label: Wide upper spacing

sections.title: Weights

fields.help: How much to favor doubling the root when there are more voices than chord tones, per extra copy. Positive encourages it, negative avoids it.
fields.label: Root

fields.help: How much to favor doubling the fifth when there are more voices than chord tones, per extra copy. Positive encourages it, negative avoids it.
fields.label: Fifth

fields.help: How much to favor doubling the third when there are more voices than chord tones, per extra copy. Positive encourages it, negative avoids it.
fields.label: Third

fields.help: How much to favor doubling the seventh when there are more voices than chord tones, per extra copy. Positive encourages it, negative avoids it.
fields.label: Seventh

fields.help: How much to favor doubling the color when there are more voices than chord tones, per extra copy. Positive encourages it, negative avoids it.
fields.label: Color

fields.help: How much to favor doubling the extension when there are more voices than chord tones, per extra copy. Positive encourages it, negative avoids it.
fields.label: Extension

fields.help: How reluctant the picker is to drop the root when there are fewer voices than chord tones. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Root

fields.help: How reluctant the picker is to drop the third when there are fewer voices than chord tones. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Third

fields.help: How reluctant the picker is to drop the fifth when there are fewer voices than chord tones. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Fifth

fields.help: How reluctant the picker is to drop the seventh when there are fewer voices than chord tones. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Seventh

fields.help: How reluctant the picker is to drop the color when there are fewer voices than chord tones. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Color

fields.help: How reluctant the picker is to drop the extension when there are fewer voices than chord tones. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Extension

fields.help: How much to favor root position (the root in the bass). Not used for slash chords, whose bass is fixed. Higher is more preferred; 0 is neutral.
fields.label: Root

fields.help: How much to favor first inversion (the third in the bass). Not used for slash chords, whose bass is fixed. Higher is more preferred; 0 is neutral.
fields.label: First

fields.help: How much to favor second inversion (the fifth in the bass; also a 6th, sus tone or extension in the bass). Not used for slash chords, whose bass is fixed. Higher is more preferred; 0 is neutral.
fields.label: Second

fields.help: How much to favor third inversion (the 7th in the bass). Not used for slash chords, whose bass is fixed. Higher is more preferred; 0 is neutral.
fields.label: Third

fields.default: E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4
fields.help: Open-string pitches in string order, starting with the string you strum first (the thickest on a guitar), so a ukulele is G4 C4 E4 A4. 3 to 12 strings. Required.
fields.hint: (note names or MIDI numbers, e.g. E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4)
fields.label: Strings

fields.help: Highest fret the picker will reach; higher allows shapes further up the neck.
fields.label: Max fret

fields.help: How many fretting fingers the hand has available.
fields.label: Fingers

fields.help: Widest fret stretch the hand holds on a normal pass.
fields.label: Max span

fields.help: Widest stretch accepted as a last resort when no shape fits Max span; must be at least Max span.
fields.label: Relaxed span

fields.help: Whether one finger flattened across several strings can stand in for several fretted fingers at once.
fields.label: Allow barre chords

sections.blurb: Each weight adds to a voicing's score, so a higher number always means more preferred. Positive values pull the picker toward a trait; negative values push it away. Zero is neutral. The defaults suit most music, so change these only if the results aren't to your taste.

fields.help: How the picker treats strings that actually sound. More positive favors fuller-sounding fingerings; negative would favor sparser ones.
fields.label: Sounding string

fields.help: How the picker treats open strings (fret 0), on top of the sounding-string weight. More positive favors open strings.
fields.label: Open string

fields.help: How the picker treats the root as the lowest-sounding note, judged by pitch, not string. Added when it is and subtracted when it isn't; more positive insists on a root bass.
fields.label: Correct bass note

fields.help: How the picker treats a slash chord's named bass (the G in C/G) as the lowest-sounding note, judged by pitch. Added when it is and subtracted when it isn't; more positive insists on it.
fields.label: Correct slash bass

fields.help: How the picker treats each fret between a shape's lowest and highest fretted notes (open strings don't count). More negative favors compact shapes.
fields.label: Wide stretch

fields.help: How the picker treats a shape's overall fret span beyond a single fret. More negative favors compact shapes; a one-fret span costs nothing.
fields.label: Compact shape

fields.help: How the picker treats a shape spanning exactly three frets (say 2 to 5), unless one finger on an outer string makes the reach and the rest stay within a fret of the lowest. Set strongly negative to reject shapes no hand can hold.
fields.label: Awkward stretch

fields.help: How the picker treats fingerings further up the neck. More negative keeps fingerings closer to the nut.
fields.label: High neck position

fields.help: How the picker treats each fretted string; a barre counts every string it holds down. More negative favors shapes with more open or muted strings.
fields.label: Fretted finger

fields.help: How the picker treats a shape that frets more strings than there are fingers, so it needs a barre; charged once, on top of the fretted-finger weight. More negative avoids barres.
fields.label: Barre

fields.help: How the picker treats a muted string buried between two sounding strings. More negative avoids that shape.
fields.label: Muted inner string

fields.help: How the picker treats the hand shifting from the previous chord, across the whole song. More negative steadies the hand.
fields.label: Hand movement

fields.help: How the picker treats a finger staying on the same string and fret between chords. More positive rewards keeping it there.
fields.label: Kept finger

sections.title: Weights

fields.help: Lowest note the left hand may play (note name or MIDI number).
fields.label: Low

fields.help: Highest note the left hand may play (note name or MIDI number).
fields.label: High

rows.help: Lowest note the left hand may play (note name or MIDI number).
rows.label: Left hand

fields.help: Lowest note of the right-hand range, used only by the fallback voicing; the RH lowest-note anchor sets where the right hand really starts.
fields.label: Low

fields.help: Highest note the right hand may play (note name or MIDI number).
fields.label: High

rows.help: Lowest note of the right-hand range, used only by the fallback voicing; the RH lowest-note anchor sets where the right hand really starts.
rows.label: Right hand

fields.help: Lowest note of the preferred bass register. Sitting below it costs the bass-below-range weight per semitone.
fields.label: Low

fields.help: Highest note of the preferred bass register. Sitting above it costs the bass-above-range weight per semitone.
fields.label: High

rows.help: Lowest note of the preferred bass register. Sitting below it costs the bass-below-range weight per semitone.
rows.label: Bass (preferred)

fields.help: Lowest pitch the right hand's bottom note may sit on; a hard limit.
fields.label: Low

fields.help: Highest pitch the right hand's bottom note may sit on; a hard limit.
fields.label: High

rows.help: Lowest pitch the right hand's bottom note may sit on; a hard limit.
rows.label: RH lowest-note anchor

fields.help: Target for the right hand's mean pitch. Drifting from it costs the right-hand center weight per semitone.
fields.label: RH center

fields.help: Neighbouring right-hand notes 4 semitones or less apart, with the lower one below this note, count as muddy and cost the muddy-low-interval weight.
fields.label: Muddy floor

fields.help: Widest reach of the right hand, in semitones (a ninth by default); extensions that won't fit are dropped. The left hand plays one bass note or an octave.
fields.label: Hand span

fields.help: Most notes the right hand may play at once; extensions are dropped first. The left hand plays one bass note or an octave.
fields.label: Max notes/hand

fields.help: Most notes both hands may play together.
fields.label: Max total notes

fields.help: The right hand's lowest note should sit more than this many semitones above the left hand's top note, or it costs the hands-too-close weight.
fields.label: Hand gap floor

fields.help: Whether the left hand plays a bass note. Off, the right hand plays alone, so a slash chord's bass note isn't heard.
fields.label: Add bass note

sections.blurb: Each weight adds to a voicing's score, so a higher number always means more preferred. Positive values pull the picker toward a trait; negative values push it away. Zero is neutral. The defaults suit most music, so change these only if the results aren't to your taste.

fields.help: How the picker treats a note kept in the right hand. More positive favors fuller voicings; negative would favor sparser ones.
fields.label: Right-hand note

fields.help: How the picker treats the right hand's mean pitch straying from its target center. More negative keeps it closer to center.
fields.label: Right-hand center

fields.help: How the picker treats the bass sitting below the preferred bass range. More negative discourages a bass that's too low.
fields.label: Bass below range

fields.help: How the picker treats the bass sitting above the preferred bass range. More negative discourages a bass that's too high.
fields.label: Bass above range

fields.help: How the picker treats octave-doubling the bass note. More negative avoids doubling it.
fields.label: Doubled bass

fields.help: How the picker treats an octave-doubled bass sitting below the preferred bass range, on top of the doubling weight. More negative avoids it.
fields.label: Doubled bass low

fields.help: How the picker treats neighbouring right-hand notes 4 semitones or less apart whose lower note is below the muddy floor, per pair. More negative avoids muddy low intervals.
fields.label: Muddy low interval

fields.help: How the picker treats a right-hand gap wider than an octave. Rarely applies: the right hand is stacked within an octave, so only the fallback voicing can leave such a gap.
fields.label: Wide right-hand gap

fields.help: How the picker treats the right hand sitting within the hand gap floor of the left hand's top note, per semitone. More negative keeps the hands apart.
fields.label: Hands too close

fields.help: How the picker treats a note holding the same pitch across a chord change. More positive rewards holding common tones.
fields.label: Common tone held

fields.help: How the picker treats a note's nearest-neighbour movement across a chord change, across the whole song. More negative steadies the voicing.
fields.label: Voice movement

fields.help: How much the picker loses when the root is missing from both hands; the right hand may leave out the fifth, or extensions that won't fit. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Root

fields.help: How much the picker loses when the third is missing from both hands; the right hand may leave out the fifth, or extensions that won't fit. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Third

fields.help: How much the picker loses when the fifth is missing from both hands; the right hand may leave out the fifth, or extensions that won't fit. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Fifth

fields.help: How much the picker loses when the seventh is missing from both hands; the right hand may leave out the fifth, or extensions that won't fit. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Seventh

fields.help: How much the picker loses when the color is missing from both hands; the right hand may leave out the fifth, or extensions that won't fit. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Color

fields.help: How much the picker loses when the extension is missing from both hands; the right hand may leave out the fifth, or extensions that won't fit. More negative keeps it; nearer zero allows dropping it.
fields.label: Extension
